chapter_seo_title: Li Huowang Forges a Human-Skin Artifact and Has a Heart-to-Heart with Li Sui
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang crafts a second human-skin artifact, teaching Li Sui talismans while navigating fatherhood, freedom, and his revulsion for leeches.
og_title: Li Huowang Forges a Second Human-Skin Artifact — And Learns What It Means to Raise a Daughter
og_description: Between mercury baths and flesh stitching, Li Huowang has the hardest parenting conversation of his life with a daughter made of tentacles.
twitter_title: Li Huowang: “You’re not human.” Li Sui: “If I’m nice, will they stop being scared?” 💔
twitter_description: The quietest chapter of Dao Gui Yi Xian hits harder than most battles—Li Sui asks the big questions.

lore_anchors.definition: A collection of talisman-drawing techniques and formulas, originally given to Li Huowang by a blind fortune-teller.
A classic Daoist protective mantra, chanted to shield the practitioner from harm during dangerous rituals.
A blood-sucking worm found in rice paddies, locally known as “cow rot-crotch”; a mundane pest that triggers Li Huowang’s rare disgust.

surfaces: True Sutra of the Fire Vestments
lore_anchors.definition: The Ao-Jing sect’s sacred text; when burned, releases a healing slug that seals wounds with agonizing pain.
A parasitic entity born from corrupted cultivation; Li Sui’s true nature.
